findings.title: Backup-code login is case-sensitive while codes are presented as uppercase-style codes
findings.body: Backup codes are generated as lowercase hex in the setup endpoint, displayed/copyable as XXXXX-XXXXX, and this login check only strips '-' before doing backupCodes.indexOf(...). If a user transcribes a valid code in uppercase (a-f become A-F), or an authenticator/backup note uppercases it, indexOf returns -1 and a valid single-use code is rejected with IncorrectBackupCode. The lookup should normalize the submitted code (e.g. trim and toLowerCase) before comparison.

findings.title: Disabling 2FA with a backup code has the same case-sensitivity bug
findings.body: This endpoint computes backupCodes.indexOf(req.body.backupCode.replaceAll('-', '')) without lowercasing/trimming. A correctly transcribed backup code entered in uppercase therefore returns IncorrectBackupCode, so a user who has lost their authenticator cannot disable 2FA with a valid code. Normalize the input the same way codes are generated/stored before checking membership.

findings.title: Single-use backup codes can be replayed concurrently
findings.body: Authorize reads user.backupCodes, checks indexOf, then later does a separate prisma.user.update setting backupCodes[index] = null. There is no atomic/conditional update or transaction locking the row between check and consumption. Two parallel login attempts using the same backup code can both read the pre-consumption array, both pass indexOf, and both be authenticated before either update lands, violating the documented 'each backup code can be used exactly once' guarantee. Consumption must be atomic (e.g. conditional update/transaction) so only one request can claim a code.

findings.title: Parent is only notified of enabled 2FA when the backup-code Close button is clicked
findings.body: On successful enable, handleEnable now only advances to DisplayBackupCodes instead of calling onEnable(). onEnable() is invoked solely from the backup-codes Close button. If the user dismisses the dialog via the Dialog's onOpenChange path (X button, outside click, Escape) after the server has already set twoFactorEnabled=true, the parent/security page is never refreshed and resetState() is not run, leaving the UI showing 2FA as disabled (and stale secret/backup-code state in the modal) until a full reload. The dialog-close path should perform the same completion/cleanup as the Close button.

findings.title: External IdP users in the totpEmail flow cannot reach the backup-code option
findings.body: When totpEmail is present (the flow used for Google/SAML users who have 2FA enabled), the footer is ExternalTotpFooter, which only offers Cancel, instead of TwoFactorFooter which contains the 'Lost access' toggle. The BackupCode form is rendered only when twoFactorLostAccess becomes true, and that state can never be set in this flow, even though the credentials authorize callback now supports backupCode. External-IdP 2FA users who lost their authenticator therefore still have no backup-code login path.

findings.title: Users who enabled 2FA before this feature can never obtain backup codes
findings.body: Setup returns TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled for anyone with twoFactorEnabled=true, and this PR adds no regenerate/view endpoint or settings action. All pre-existing 2FA users therefore have backupCodes=null forever unless they disable and re-enable 2FA; if they try a backup code at login they get MissingBackupCodes, whose message says 'Please generate them in your settings' even though no such settings action exists. Add a regeneration flow for already-enabled users or change the message/flow so these users are not dead-ended.

findings.title: No test exercises actually logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code
findings.body: The added e2e coverage only clicks the backup-code download/copy buttons and checks the filename/toast during setup; the file itself notes 'TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup'. The security-critical new behavior — valid backup code logs in, the same code cannot be reused, an invalid code is rejected, and a backup code can disable 2FA — is entirely untested, so regressions in next-auth-options.ts or disable.ts would not be caught.
